tip: Dylid means one should or it should be done, with no subject named. Dylid gwarchod = should be protected.
The word o (of) triggers soft mutation on the next noun: bwyd becomes fwyd in digon o fwyd (plenty of food).
For a future if, Welsh uses bydd after os, not the present: Os bydd y trên yn llawn = if the train is full.
Us wraps the verb as ein ... ni: ein gyrru ni = drive us. The pronoun frames the verb-noun on both sides.
To take someone you say mynd â, literally go with: mynd â'r plant = take the children.
The word â triggers aspirate mutation: pobl becomes phobl in dod â phobl (bring people).
Your (informal) frames the verb as dy ... di: dy helpu di = help you. Formal or plural uses eich ... chi instead.
After a number Welsh keeps the noun singular: chwe mis = six months (month), never a plural.
meddai means said or says and reports speech, placed after the quote: meddai'r meddyg = the doctor says.
pan (when) triggers soft mutation on the verb: cyrhaedda becomes gyrhaedda in pan gyrhaedda i (when I arrive).
His shortens to 'i and triggers soft mutation: prawf becomes brawf in pasio'i brawf (pass his test).
For unreal or hypothetical ifs use Pe with bawn, not os: Pe bawn i'n gwybod = if I had known.
To report that something is, use fod: Dywedodd rhywun fod y bws yn hwyr = someone said the bus was late.
To say on a day, soft-mutate dydd to ddydd: ddydd Mercher = on Wednesday.
The word yn meaning in triggers nasal mutation: drama becomes nrama in yn nrama'r ysgol (in the school play).
To rain is bwrw glaw, literally throw rain: Os bydd hi'n bwrw glaw = if it rains.
Welsh builds the passive with cael plus ei: bydd y wers yn cael ei chanslo = the lesson will be cancelled.
In old names son of is fab, a mutation of mab: Math fab Mathonwy = Math son of Mathonwy.
my (fy) triggers nasal mutation on the next word: fy niwtor = my tutor.
Welsh shows having with gyda, not a verb: amser gyda fi = time with me, meaning I have time.
Another way to say has is Mae gan: Mae gan Gymru hunaniaeth = Wales has an identity.
